page: Amazon Web Services c4.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance belonging to the c4 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor with an x86_64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 2.9 GHz. This instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, utilizing hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. It is configured with 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding 1.88 GB of RAM per core. The CPU features a 25 MB L3 cache, 32 KB L1d cache, and 0.25 MB L2 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instructions.

The c4.4xlarge instance operates on the Xen hypervisor. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached options. Networking capabilities include a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps. The instance does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the c4.4xlarge in the average performance tier across multiple metrics. It achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1440.69 and a multi-core score of 15219.95. Memory bandwidth tests show cached small-block read speeds of 851.49 GB/sec and uncached large-block read speeds of 89.52 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the instance handles 6.16 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 11.52 GB/sec. For machine learning tasks, it processes 7B model prompts at 23.37 tokens/sec and generates text at 10.7 tokens/sec. This hardware profile is suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, and web serving, where dedicated CPU resources are required but local storage is not a necessity.
